_readme: Fill in 'contrasts' BEFORE you look at launch check results. Each entry: pillar, group_a, group_b, expected ('a_higher' or 'b_higher'), min_gap (points, the smallest mean gap that counts as passing), reason (why you expect it, ideally with a source). A group selects places by any of: area_type, metro, state, or an explicit list 'places' of 'metro|name'. Use contrasts you are certain of; the check is a tripwire for data or logic problems, not a target to tune toward. Entries under '_examples' are ignored. 'expected_uniform' lists sub-metrics (pillar, path_prefix, optional metros, reason) that are uniform within a metro by design, so the degenerate-metro section does not show them; leave it empty until you have decided which findings are by design.

contrasts.reason: Rural areas are sparse and far from major hospitals and hospital networks (owner, very sure).
There is almost no public transit in exurban areas (owner, very sure).
Rural areas have very small towns with limited options, or places are spread out (owner, very sure).
Airports are built near cities, even when some sit far out, like Denver (owner, sure).
Most jobs are in cities, and rural workers commute into cities (owner, very sure). Small gap because the pillar has little spread.
Homes are cheaper relative to income in rural areas than in expensive metros; some metros and some rural areas are exceptions (owner, very sure).
More concrete in cities; some cities invest in trees, parks and waterfronts, so the gap is small (owner, sure).
Same statement for exurban areas (owner, sure).
Denver sits next to the Rockies (trails, skiing, mountain parks); Houston is flat and hot and humid with far fewer trail and ski options (drafted by Claude at the owner's request; owner to confirm).

_examples.reason: Hospital and clinic counts and distances differ by an order of magnitude between dense cores and rural areas.
Example of a named place against a group (a named group needs at least 10 places to be evaluated).

_expected_uniform_example.reason: Market-quality components come from metro-level data, so places in one metro share them by design (tracker D8).
